result:
Task 12 is complete, committed and merged to `main`.

## What now exists

`sql/migrations/0005_flatten_layer.sql` — eight **plain views** over `helena_normalized_events`:

| View | One row per |
| --- | --- |
| `helena_flatten_flows` | normalized event — the flow, typed |
| `helena_flatten_dns` | event that observed DNS (rcode + counts) |
| `helena_flatten_dns_queries` / `_dns_responses` | question asked / resource record answered |
| `helena_flatten_tls` | event that observed TLS (SNI, versions, client & server fingerprints) |
| `helena_flatten_http` | observed HTTP layer, per version |
| `helena_flatten_http_requests` / `_http_responses` | request / response, HTTP/1 and HTTP/2 in one view with a `protocol` column |

Every row carries tenant, sensor, capture sha256, record offset, event id and schema version.

## The two things that were measured rather than assumed

**Nothing is materialized**, and that is only free if the signal layer can still stream over a plain view. Measured against RisingWave 3.0.3 first: a materialized view over these views backfills and returns rows — including over `jsonb_array_elements(...) WITH ORDINALITY` and over a `UNION ALL` of two such branches — and `TUMBLE(helena_flatten_flows, flow_start, INTERVAL '5 minutes')` is accepted directly off the plain view (the 62-record sample splits 59/3 across 21:35:00Z).

**Absence stays distinct from emptiness.** A set-returning function collapses "array was empty" and "layer never observed" into the same zero rows, so each layer family gets an observation row whose *existence* is the statement of observation and whose count column may read 0. `tcp.24` has a TLS row reading `alpn_count = 0`; `udp.28` appears in none of the seven.

## Verification

`uv run pytest -q` → **480 passed** (36 new, all by execution against a throwaway engine: real migrations, real Normalizer/EventStore, real records). `make check` passes. Four mutation checks were run and each watched to fail — one of them found a real gap: summing HTTP counts over the sample could not tell `request_count` from `response_count`, because all eleven HTTP/1 observations hold as many responses as requests. That is now covered by a per-row comparison plus a temporary capture holding a real record with a shortened response list.

One negative result recorded honestly in the report, and one decision record written (`docs/decisions/0015-the-flatten-layer.md`). No escalations, no invariant conflicts. Report at `prds/reports/task-12.json`, status `completed`.
